title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Elena Park
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page codifies the operating procedures and canonical artifacts for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is consistent, discoverable, and low-friction docs that reduce time-to-value for external and internal developers and reduce repetitive support work.

Audience: DevEx engineers, technical writers, solutions engineers, SDK maintainers, developer advocates, and support engineers.

Owner & Contacts
- Primary owner: DevEx Documentation (engineering)
- Content owner: Elena Park (author)
- SDK maintainers: see individual SDK headers in the docs
- Support escalation: support@redwood-inference.internal (follow escalation playbook)

High-level principles
- Single source of truth: every SDK guide, quickstart and API example must have a canonical page that is referenced by tutorials, sample apps, and PRs.
- Low-friction onboarding: Quickstarts must be runnable in <10 minutes (including sign-up/credentials) and include code blocks for copy-paste.
- Reproducible examples: examples must include explicit dependency versions and environment variables.
- Observable fixes: top support issues and canonical fixes must be triaged, documented, and linked from SDK pages.

1) Docs site operating procedures (publishing workflow)

Purpose: ensure changes to public-facing docs are reviewed, tested, and deployed with clear ownership and rollback steps.

Publishing workflow (step-by-step):
1. Draft locally in Markdown/respective template. Include frontmatter: title, summary, date, owner, labels.
2. Open a PR against docs repo: docs.redwood-inference (branch: devex/docs/<short-title>).
3. Automated checks run: linting, link-checker, code sample validation (unit tests for sample apps).
4. Reviewer assignment: at least one DevEx reviewer + one SDK owner for code changes.
5. Merge and CI deploy to staging site (docs-staging.redwood-inference.com).
6. Smoke test on staging (basic link crawl + run 1-2 quickstarts via CI runners).
7. Mark the PR with "ready-to-publish" label. Release engineer schedules the release window if it affects stable quickstarts.
8. Deploy to production site during the next docs deployment window (see release cadence below).
9. If an issue is found after deploy: revert PR (hotfix) and notify #devex-docs on Slack; file a post-issue doc update.

Release cadence and windows:
- Minor content updates: weekly (Tuesdays 06:00-08:00 UTC).
- Quickstart or sample app updates that change CLI or authentication flows: must be scheduled in the weekly run and flagged in release notes.
- Breaking or migration changes: require a 2-week deprecation notice and cross-team review.

Authoring checklist (required in PR description):
- Summary and purpose (one paragraph)
- Owner and reviewers listed
- Compatibility statement (SDK versions, API versions)
- Smoke-test steps and links to test logs
- Accessibility check (alt text, headings)
- Labels and related pages set

2) SDK guide standards and template

Every SDK guide must follow the standard template below. Use the SDK template file: /repos/docs/templates/sdk-guide.md

Template sections (must appear in order):
- Title and one-line summary
- Use cases and when to pick this SDK
- Install instructions (pin versions)
- Quickstart (copy-paste runnable example)
- Authentication and configuration (env vars, config file examples)
- Common patterns and best practices (batching, retries, backoff)
- Error handling and mapping to HTTP status codes (examples)
- Top support issues (linked to canonical fixes)
- API reference snippet (link to auto-generated reference)
- Migration notes (for breaking changes)
- Maintenance & release notes (owner, release cadence)

Example: Python SDK quickstart snippet

Prereqs: Python 3.10+, pip

Copy-paste:
```
# Install
pip install redwood-inference-sdk==1.4.2

# Simple text generation
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-large-1", prompt="Translate to French: 'Hello world'")
print(resp.text)
```

Environment variables to document exactly:
- REDWOOD_API_KEY (scoped to project)
- REDWOOD_REGION (optional; default: us-west-2)

3) Quickstarts & templates library

Goal: provide runnable minimal apps and opinionated templates developers can fork. Quickstarts live in docs + sample-apps repo and must include CI-run smoke tests.

Required quickstart types:
- Hello World (text generation)
- Chat app (browser + backend streaming example)
- Embeddings + vector search (Python + Node)
- Streaming file ingestion and summarization
- On-prem private deployment quickstart (VPC + KMS integration example)

Quickstart structure (repo + docs):
- README.md (purpose, runtime, deploy steps)
- explicit pinned deps: requirements.txt or package.json
- .env.example with all env vars
- automated CI workflow (smoke-test)
- LICENSE and CONTRIBUTING

Template examples (convention):
- template/sdk-basic-boilerplate (small library scaffold)
- template/oss-example-app (MIT-licensed demo)

4) API examples and coding patterns

Best-practices to include in examples:
- Use streaming where low latency is required; show both streaming and non-streaming examples.
- Show function/tool-calling examples for structured outputs.
- Demonstrate retries and idempotency for rate-limited endpoints.

Common examples to publish (must have both REST and SDK variants):
- Text generation (curl + Python + Node)
- Chat with system/messages history
- Call a tool (structured JSON output) and parse to typed objects
- Embeddings generation and upsert to a vector store (sample integrations with Weaviate and Milvus)
- Reranking flow (embeddings similarity + model rerank)

HTTP example (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "redwood-medium-1", "prompt": "Summarize: Redwood Inference platform"}'
```

Node SDK example (snippet):
```
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello' }] });
console.log(res.text);
```

5) Top support issues and canonical fixes (living table)

Maintain a surfaced, searchable list of the most frequent support tickets that relate to docs or SDKs. Each entry must include: symptom, root cause, immediate workaround, long-term fix, owner, and links to PRs or code. Update monthly.

Table: top issues (example rows)
| issue_id | symptom | root_cause | immediate_workaround | long_term_fix | owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DX-001 | SDK fails with "401 Unauthorized" after token rotation | Clients using static token in env var after key rotation | Re-authenticate, rotate env var and restart process | Add SDK auto-refresh + clear error message; document rotation steps | Priya Mehta |
| DX-002 | Streaming client disconnects after ~60s on some proxies | Idle connection timeouts at edge proxies | Use heartbeat ping or chunked keep-alive; shorten keepalive interval | Add reconnect/backoff in sample client; update quickstart | Jared Klein |
| DX-003 | Embeddings similarity returns low-quality matches | Users sending raw text without normalization | Document normalization + provide a helper util in SDK | Add embedding preprocessing utility and tests | Sofia Alvarez |

Canonical fix template (use when authoring a fix):
- Ticket link: [internal]
- Symptom: one-line
- Root cause: analysis + logs
- Workaround: steps
- PRs: links
- Tests: unit/integration tests added
- Rollout plan: canary > full > monitor metrics (errors, latency, quality)

6) On-call & escalation linkage

If a published doc causes a regression or break (e.g., breaking auth flow):
1. Tag #devex-docs and on-call support engineer.
2. Follow the incident playbook: create incident, triage, rollback docs PR if necessary.
3. Postmortem within 72 hours if customer impact.

7) Measurement & success signals

Track the following metrics (owner: DevEx analytics):
- Time-to-first-successful-request for new users (measured via quickstart CI): target < 10 minutes.
- Number of repeating support tickets referencing docs: target -30% YoY.
- Search-to-page success rate in docs site (search result -> page with click + successful quickstart run): target 70%+
- SDK adoption and downloads by language (monthly active repos)

8) FAQ (common author questions)
- Q: How do I mark a page as "stable" vs "experimental"?
  A: Use the label "stable" and include compatibility block in header; set deprecation timeline for experimental features.
- Q: Who approves API example changes that touch billing/auth flows?
  A: DevEx + Security + Billing reviewers are required.

Appendix: Useful links and templates
- SDK guide template: /repos/docs/templates/sdk-guide.md
- Quickstart template: /repos/sample-apps/quickstart-template/README.md
- Docs linting and link checker job: .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml
- DevEx docs Slack channel: #devex-docs
